passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) is intended to help you understand FTAI Aviation Ltd. (the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”). Our MD&A should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes, and with Part I, Item 1A, “Risk Factors” and “Forward-Looking Statements” included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. A discussion of our cash flows for 2025 compared to 2024 is included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 , under Part II, Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations. Overview We are a leading independent engine maintenance platform focused on the CFM56-5B, CFM56-7B and V2500 aircraft engines which power the 737NG and A320ceo aircraft. We repair and rebuild engines in our maintenance facilities and with our joint venture partners, and sell or lease the engines to airlines and asset owners around the world. Our primary business model is to sell or lease engines via exchange through our proprietary Maintenance, Repair and Exchange (“MRE”) model which is reported under our Aerospace Products segment. We also own and manage a portfolio of on- and off-lease aircraft and engines through our Aviation Leasing segment. While historically these investment activities have been primarily held on balance sheet, at the end of 2024, we launched our Strategic Capital Initiative, which consists of an asset management business that manages third-party capital to invest in on-lease aircraft and engines. We expect our primary investment activities to be through our Strategic Capital Initiative going forward. As of December 31, 2025, we had total consolidated assets of $4.4 billion and total equity of $334.2 million. Internalization of Management On May 28, 2024, the Company entered into definitive agreements with the Former Manager and Master GP to internalize the Company’s management function. As part of the termination of the Management Agreement, the Company (i) paid the Former Manager (for itself and on behalf of the Master GP, as applicable) the Cash Consideration, the compensation accrued and payable, but not yet paid, under the Management Agreement and the expenses that were reimbursable, but not yet reimbursed, under the Management Agreement; (ii) issued to the Former Manager (for itself and on behalf of the Master GP, as applicable) the Share Consideration; and (iii) purchased from Master GP all of its partnership interests in FTAI Aviation Holdco Ltd., a subsidiary of the Company, in exchange for $30 thousand. Following the Internalization, the Company no longer pays management fees or incentive distributions to the Former Manager and Master GP. In connection with the termination of the Management Agreement, the Company also entered into a Transition Services Agreement with the Former Manager. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider the following risks and other information in this Form 10-K in evaluating us and our shares. Any of the following risks, as well as additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial, could materially and adversely affect our results of operations or financial condition. The risk factors generally have been separated into the following categories: risks related to our business, risks related to taxation and risks related to the Company’s shares. However, these categories do overlap and should not be considered exclusive. Risks Related to Our Business Uncertainty relating to macroeconomic conditions, including those that affect the commercial aviation industry, may reduce the demand for our assets, result in non-performance of contracts by our lessees or charterers, limit our ability to obtain additional capital to finance new investments, or have other unforeseen negative effects. Uncertainty and negative trends in general economic conditions in the United States and abroad, including significant tightening of credit markets and commodity price volatility, historically have created and continue to create difficult operating environments for owners and operators in the aviation industry. As a provider of products and services to the commercial aviation industry, we are greatly affected by the overall economic conditions and other trends that affect our customers and lessees in that industry, 8 including any projected market growth that may not materialize or be sustainable and any lasting effects of tariffs. The commercial aviation industry is historically cyclical and has been negatively affected in the past, and could be negatively affected in future periods, by geopolitical events, natural disasters, pandemics, supply chain disruptions, labor issues, environmental concerns (including climate change), lack of capital, cost inflation, and weak or volatile economic conditions. A number of governments have implemented, or are considering implementing, a broad variety of governmental actions or new regulations for the financial markets and international trade. In addition, limitations on the availability of capital, higher costs of capital for financing expenditures or the desire to preserve liquidity, may cause our current or prospective customers and lessees to make reductions in future capital budgets and spending. Further, demand for our assets is related to passenger and cargo traffic growth, which in turn is dependent on general business and economic conditions. Global economic downturns could have an adverse impact on passenger and cargo traffic levels and consequently our customers’ and lessees’ business, which may in turn result in a significant reduction in revenues, earnings and cash flows, difficulties accessing capital and a deterioration in the value of our assets. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded sharply year over year and sits well above the sector median, reflecting the high-margin engine exchange model and a mix shift toward Aerospace Products rather than leasing. This earnings power is the primary buffer against the negative cash conversion discussed below.

Gross leverage fell by roughly half versus the prior year and now sits modestly above the sector median, while net leverage remains just inside the next risk-band boundary. The improvement reflects EBITDA growth rather than debt reduction, since borrowings were broadly flat year over year.

key_risks.text: Operating cash flow is negative and deteriorated for a second consecutive year, driven by working capital absorbed into engine inventory and exchange assets. Cash conversion is far below the sector median, so reported earnings are not currently translating into cash available for creditors.

The debt stack is entirely unsecured senior notes with no borrowings drawn on the revolver, and no maturities fall due within the next two years. However, a large bullet falls in year three and the remainder is back-end loaded, concentrating refinancing risk in a single window.

The risk factors flag cyclical aviation demand, lease counterparty non-performance and constrained capital access as core exposures. Because the platform sells and leases engines to airlines, a traffic downturn would pressure both asset values and lessee collections simultaneously.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved materially year over year and comfortably exceeds one times, but remains well below the sector median. With interest expense running at a meaningful share of operating income, coverage has limited cushion if engine margins normalize or rates reset higher on refinancing.

Liquidity is strong on a balance-sheet basis, with the current ratio far above the sector median and a large undrawn revolver. That said, the cash buffer is modest relative to total debt, and free cash flow is negative, so debt service currently depends on refinancing access rather than internally generated cash.

overall_credit_view.text: The credit profile is a growth-funded, asset-heavy engine platform: strong margins and improving leverage, offset by persistent negative operating cash flow and distributions that exceed internally generated funds. Leverage sits above the sector median but is trending down, leaving thin headroom to the next risk band.

Our forward view is stable-to-improving, contingent on working capital normalizing as the exchange model scales and on orderly refinancing of the year-three bullet. A sustained cash burn or a leveraged acquisition would erode the current cushion; absent that, coverage and leverage trends support the present profile.

credit_strengths.text: 經營利潤率按年大幅擴張，並顯著高於行業中位數，反映高利潤率的引擎交換模式，以及產品組合由租賃轉向航空航天產品的變化。此盈利能力是下文所述負現金轉換的主要緩衝。
總槓桿較上年下降約一半，目前略高於行業中位數，而淨槓桿仍僅處於下一個風險區間邊界之內。改善反映的是EBITDA增長而非債務減少，因為借款按年大致持平。

key_risks.text: 經營現金流為負，且連續第二年惡化，原因是營運資金被吸收至引擎存貨及交換資產。現金轉換遠低於行業中位數，因此報告盈利目前並未轉化為可供債權人使用的現金。
債務結構全為無抵押優先票據，循環信貸額度並無提取借款，且未來兩年內並無到期債務。然而，一筆大額子彈還款於第三年到期，其餘則集中於後期，令再融資風險集中於單一窗口。
風險因素將週期性航空需求、租賃交易對手不履約及資本獲取受限列為核心風險敞口。由於平台向航空公司出售及租賃引擎，航空交通量下滑將同時對資產價值及承租人收款構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年顯著改善，並穩妥超過一倍，但仍遠低於行業中位數。由於利息開支佔經營收入相當比重，若引擎利潤率正常化或再融資時利率重定於更高水平，覆蓋率的緩衝有限。
資產負債表層面的流動性強勁，流動比率遠高於行業中位數，且循環信貸額度大部分未提取。儘管如此，現金緩衝相對總債務規模有限，且自由現金流為負，因此償債目前依賴再融資渠道而非內部產生現金。

overall_credit_view.text: 信貸狀況為一個以增長融資、資產密集的引擎平台：利潤率強勁且槓桿改善，但被持續負經營現金流及超出內部產生資金的分派所抵銷。槓桿高於行業中位數但呈下降趨勢，距下一個風險區間僅餘有限空間。
我們的前瞻觀點為穩定至改善，取決於營運資金隨交換模式擴大而正常化，以及第三年子彈還款有序再融資。持續現金消耗或槓桿收購將侵蝕現有緩衝；若無此情況，覆蓋率及槓桿趨勢支持目前狀況。
